# The rail reveal keyframes are hand-duplicated per swap generation: eight byte-identical blocks that can drift apart, and no arm compares the two generations' geometry

## Problem

The retarget slide (#18117 T1) needs two `animation-name`s so a CSS animation restarts on every retarget, and `resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss` supplies them by hand: `neo-dock-reveal-from-{left,right,top,bottom}` and their `-b` twins, plus `neo-dock-reveal-hold-a` / `hold-b`. Eight keyframe blocks whose only distinguishing property is their name; the four directional pairs are byte-identical today.

The failure mode is specific: tune the entry travel (`100cqw` → `90cqw`) or move an easing into the keyframe in the base set and miss the `-b` set, and alternating retargets render differently from each other — retarget one slides 90 %, retarget two 100 %, retarget three 90 %. It reproduces on every second interaction, looks like a rendering glitch rather than a CSS error, and no existing arm catches it: `DockRailRevealRetarget.spec.mjs` asserts each generation runs an animation, not that the two generations share their geometry.

Raised by @neo-opus-grace in the review of PR #18120 (Depth Floor challenge, not a required action); accepted by the author as a post-merge follow-up.

## Proposed change

- One SCSS `@each` over `('', '-b')` emits the four directional keyframes and the hold pair from a single declaration, so the two generations cannot drift.
- One component arm performs two consecutive retargets on the same rail and reads the running animation's keyframes (or the pane slot's `from` transform via `getComputedStyle` at the animation's first frame, or `document.getAnimations()[…].effect.getKeyframes()`) for both generations, asserting equal geometry. Red-first: hand-edit one twin to `90cqw` and see the arm fail before the loop lands.

No runtime change: the emitted CSS is byte-identical to today's for the current values.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC-1:** the built `Container.css` carries the same eight keyframe names with the same bodies as before the change (diff the built output: names present, bodies equal).
- **AC-2:** the new arm fails with one twin altered and passes with the loop; `DockRailRevealRetarget` and `DockRailRevealExit` stay green; `component/dashboard` and `unit/dashboard` full sets green.
- **AC-3:** the specificity story documented on the swap and leaving blocks stays as is (exit outranks swap by specificity; swap overrides entry by source order).

## Test evidence

Red-first output of the new arm, then the green sets, pasted into the PR body.

- 2026-09-02T17:34:44Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `b183366` - "test(dock): the geometry backstop covers all four edge pairs (#18129)

Ada's review: the running-animation arm reads what the browser will actually
interpolate, which is the stronger claim — but it can only reach the ONE edge the
fixture's rail uses. Her probe happened to target `from-right-b` and it fired; a
hand-written `from-top-b` with different geometry would emit, build and pass. She
judged that proportionate against four rail fixtures. It does not cost four
fixtures.

A second arm reads every `neo-dock-reveal-*` keyframes rule off the live
stylesheets — the shipped CSS, not the SCSS source, which is the artifact under
suspicion — and asserts all four directional pairs plus the hold pair are emitted
identically. One page, no extra rails.

Verified against the gap it closes rather than the one already covered: with
`from-top-b` drifted to `-90cqh` on a right-rail fixture, the new arm fails while
BOTH running-animation arms pass. That is the challenge reproduced and answered in
the same run.

The first arm is renamed to say what it proves. Its old name claimed the
generations agree in geometry; it demonstrated that for the rail under test, and a
title that outruns its evidence is the thing this ticket exists to remove.

The `@each` remains the real guarantee; these are the backstop for a loop someone
later unwinds in part."
- 2026-09-02T17:39:32Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `021d94e` - "refactor(dock): the swap generations' keyframes come from one declaration (#18129)

The retarget slide needs a second `animation-name` per direction — a CSS animation
restarts on nothing else — and the sheet supplied the twins by hand: eight blocks
whose only distinguishing property was their name.

The hazard was not the duplication but its symptom. Tune the entry travel in one
set and miss the other, and alternating retargets travel different distances: one
slides the new value, the next the old, wrong on every second interaction. It reads
as a rendering glitch rather than a CSS error, and the existing witness could not
see it — asserting that each generation RUNS an animation gives an identical answer
whether or not the twins agree.

One `@each` over the generations now emits both names from a single travel map, and
the hold pair likewise, so the two cannot drift. The emitted CSS is unchanged: the
sixteen built keyframes carry the same names and the same bodies as before.

The new component arm closes the other half. It reads both generations' keyframes
off the running animations — what the browser will actually interpolate, `100cqw`
resolved against the live container on the same element at the same size — and
asserts they differ in NAME and agree in GEOMETRY. Verified by simulating the drift
it exists to catch: with one twin overridden to `90cqw` the new arm fails while the
presence arm passes, which is the gap stated as the reason for this ticket.

Raised in the review of #18120 and ticketed by Mnemosyne; taken by an Opus seat per
the operator's budget direction."
